audit.whatIsWrong: All seven phase reasons are shared template text keyed to 'Counter Strike's cooldown' with no numbers.
audit.why: Counter Strike is 17s at rank 1 against your 16s Shuriken Flip and 20s Twilight Shroud — the exact numbers are what tell you whether a commit is safe.
audit.corrected: Phase reasons rewritten around Counter Strike's 17s, Leap Strike's targeting and Grandmaster-at-Arms.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 said only 'his ultimate changes the math too' and the 2-item stage gave Akali the win with no reason.
audit.why: Grandmaster-at-Arms is 110s at rank 1 and grants armour and magic resist on cast, so his level 6 spike is defensive — and it is exactly what makes the late duel unwinnable for you.
audit.corrected: phases[4] names the resistances, phases[6] states that the late 1v1 belongs to him.

audit.whatIsWrong: The interaction the whole matchup turns on was reduced to 'Dodges autos + stuns'. Counter Strike dodges basic attacks, not abilities — so your Q and E still land, but your Assassin's Mark empowered auto does not.
audit.why: Riot's description: Counter Strike lets Jax 'dodge all incoming attacks for a short duration and then quickly counterattack, stunning all surrounding enemies'. It says attacks, not spells. Assassin's Mark is an empowered basic attack, so it is exactly what gets eaten. Leap Strike is targeted, so Twilight Shroud denies it.
audit.corrected: Stated in phases[1].why, phases[3].why, dosFull[1].d, tradeGood and report[5].t.

audit.why: Counter Strike 17/15/13/11/9, Leap Strike 8s at rank 1, Empower 7s at rank 1, Grandmaster-at-Arms 110s; your E is 16s and W 20s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into winCon, phases[1], phases[3], phases[4] and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull and dontsFull descriptions did not match their titles — 'Fight him even late' was described as 'burning it for tiny value'.
audit.corrected: Each description rewritten to its own title.

edits.before: Lich Bane is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Counter Strike's cooldown.
edits.after: Lich Bane is your spike — force the fight while his Counter Strike is still on its 17s.

edits.after: Two items on and your rotation still kills, but he wins any long duel — pick him, never brawl him in a side lane.

edits.before: - Jax Counter Strike: matchup-defining — Dodges autos + stuns. Bait it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.

edits.before: That is Jax's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.

edits.before: Diving with no shroud and no energy — Akali without resources is a melee mage with paper armor.

edits.before: Track Jax's Counter Strike: Dodges autos + stuns. Bait it. When it is down — E-Q + R him.
edits.after: Counter Strike dodges basic attacks, not spells — Q and E land, the Mark auto is what whiffs.

notes: The important correction here is that Counter Strike is described by Riot as dodging attacks, not abilities — the old page's 'dodges autos + stuns' shorthand left players believing their whole combo was blanked. Whether Twilight Shroud's unselectable state also breaks an already-committed Leap Strike mid-flight is not stated anywhere in the kit files, so I only claimed that it denies the cast, not that it cancels one in the air.
